name: Link
story: The seam is the only full cut in Link, so the motion uses it as a hinge. Both yokes swing open about the seam's own right end point, where the flat edge meets the lobe arc. That end stays shut at one module while the cut opens into a wedge of 1.5 modules at the centre and 2 at the far end. Then they clap shut to exactly one module, rebound slightly, pause, and do the same beat mirrored on the seam's left end. The halves never slide apart in parallel (that's the tug) and never tip apart evenly (that's jaws). One end of the cut always holds still, like a clevis on its pin.
character: A plush quatrefoil of four round drops pressed into a square, cut once straight across and slotted halfway down each vertical. It reads as two U-links or horseshoe magnets set base to base: a clevis and its mate, a snap buckle, the two halves of a split coin. Each half on its own is a soft two-lobed bean (a pair of binoculars, a clothes-peg head, a cartoon bum), which is probably why it got rejected as "Too Friendly". The round masses are all on the outside and the square corners all point in, so it feels bubbly outside and machined inside. The name "Link" is right for the topology: two closed yokes that butt together but never interlock.
symmetry: D2, not the pure C2 the notes claim. Measured max point-set error: rot180 0.010u (path 0 maps onto path 1), mirror about x=100 0.007u (each part is also left-right symmetric by itself), mirror about y=100 0.010u (path 0 maps onto path 1). rot90 5.40u, diagonal mirror 5.39u, anti-diagonal mirror 5.40u. The outer silhouette (four identical R 19 drop-lobes at the corners of a 41.9u square) is fully 4-fold. The only thing breaking 4-fold and the diagonal mirrors is where the two 3.81u bridges sit. So the grouping into top and bottom halves is carried entirely by two 3.81 x 3.81 squares of material at (100,96.2) and (100,103.8).
construction: Measured: four lobes, each a 270 degree arc (Bezier circle fit R 18.99, max err 0.11; bbox diameter 38.09 so true R about 19.05). Centres (79.05,79.05), (120.95,79.05), (79.05,120.95), (120.95,120.95). That gives a 41.9u pitch horizontally and vertically, and a diagonal c-c of 59.25u. Every lobe's open quadrant faces (100,100) and is filled square, so each lobe is a circle with one sharp corner, and that corner sits 2.7u from centre. One module, 3.81u, sets every gap: the full-width horizontal cut (y 98.09 to 101.9), both blind slot widths (x 98.09 to 101.9), and the bridge thickness (slot ends 3.81 short of the cut: 94.28 to 98.09 and 101.9 to 105.71). Slot depth is 14.81, roughly R minus the module (19.05 - 3.81 = 15.24, off by 0.43 where the slot stops at the lobe tangent point y 120.52). Down the centre column x 98.09 to 101.9 you get a stack of bridge, gap, bridge, each 3.81 tall. Outer silhouette is an 80 x 80 square with R 19 corners that fuse along the edges, plus 3.81u notches at the top and bottom mid-edges (slot mouths) and at the left and right mid-edges (the ends of the cut). Reconciling with con/spec: the con puts only two guide circles, at (79.3,120.7) and (120.7,79.3) with R 19.3 and c-c 58.4. Measured centres are about 0.3u further out on each axis, R is about 19.05 not 19.3, and diagonal c-c is 59.25 not 58.4 (even the con's own centres give 58.55). GAP 3.8U is correct (3.81). The diagonal guide and the "two hooks, rotated 180" blurb read each half as a diagonal hook. The paths don't support that: each half is a symmetric two-lobe yoke, and the mark is two yokes back to back across one straight seam.
tensions: The weight sits in the four lobes at the corners (piece centroids at y 80.08 and 119.91, 20u out from centre). The structure sits in two tiny bridges hugging the centre. The strongest tension is the 3.81u horizontal seam, which runs clean through edge to edge: it is the only full separation in the mark, so the two halves are held together by nothing, only by being close. There is a second, quieter tension in the pairing. The outline is 4-fold, so the eye could just as easily pair the lobes left and right. Only the bridge squares decide it's top and bottom, which makes the grouping feel provisional. The blind slots are near-touches: each slot's inner walls are 3.81 apart for 14.81u and stop exactly one module short of the seam, like a cut someone stopped partway. The four square corners all point at (100,100) from 2.7u away, a converging point that nothing fills. At rest the mark already implies separating along y, opening the slots (the lobes of each yoke could pinch together), and switching partners across the seam.
parts: bottom yoke (inverted-U link): two lobes at (79.05,120.95) and (120.95,120.95) bridged along the top by a 3.81u band over a 3.81 x 14.81 blind slot that opens downward

top yoke (U link): exact 180 degree rotation (and exact y=100 mirror) of part 0; lobes at (79.05,79.05) and (120.95,79.05), bridge along the bottom edge at y 98.09, blind slot x 98.09 to 101.9 from y 60 down to 94.28, open at the top edge
ties: Hinge line = the 3.81u horizontal cut (y 98.09 to 101.9). It is the only full separation in the mark, so it is the one place two unjoined halves can pivot.

Fulcrums at F = (120.52,100) and (79.48,100), the seam's own end points. The flat seam edges only run from x 79.48 to 120.52. At those x values they meet the lobe arcs at a tangent, so these are the last points where the cut is still a straight cut. Each turn is written about C = (100,100) with offset d = (h*20.52*(1-cos a), s*20.52*sin a). The chosen end point stays fixed to 0.00002u at full open (checked numerically).

Amplitude TH = asin(1.905/41.04) = 2.661 deg, where 41.04u is the flat-seam length (fulcrum to the other seam end). Each yoke lifts the far seam end by half a module, so the cut opens by one module at that end. Measured on the real paths at full open: 3.82u at the hinge end, 5.72u at x=100 and 7.63u at the far end. That reads as 1 / 1.5 / 2 modules, the mark's own unit.

The amplitude stops short of asin(3.81/41.04) = 5.33 deg on purpose. At that angle the lobe arc just past the hinge swings into the cut and narrows it to 3.62u, below one module. At 2.661 deg the narrowest point over the whole loop is 3.76u (at x=121, f24). The yokes never touch.

Counter-rotation (top r=+TH, bottom r=-TH, offsets mirrored in y) comes from the exact mirror about y=100 (0.010u): part 1 is the reflection of part 0, so the wedge stays symmetric about the seam axis.

The second clap swaps the hinge from the right seam end to the left one. That comes from the mirror about x=100 (0.007u; each yoke is left-right symmetric by itself). The two beats measure the same wedge in mirror: 7.63 / 5.72 / 3.82u.
Both halves move at once, with no stagger. With D2 symmetry and only two parts, the top and bottom have no dial order, and a clap is a single event.
The clap closes to exactly the 3.81u rest gap and never goes past it. The yokes stay 'held together by nothing, only by being close' and never overlap.
Recoil = 0.18*TH = 0.48 deg (far end reopens to 4.49u). The blind slots already suggest springy tongs, so there is a restrained rebound after the clap, not a bounce.

Easing: GLIDE to open (a heavy lid lifting off its hinge), a short HOLD at the top, then a raw ease-in [0.55,0,0.9,0.55] to close, which speeds up into the clap and arrives at about 4.5x speed. The recoil leaves on [0.2,0.55,0.4,1], so the rebound starts with speed straight out of the impact and doesn't stick. The settle back to rest uses SOFT. p and r share every keyframe time and easing, so the engine uses native beziers.
Timing: 6f rest, 18f open, 6f hold, 8f clap, 5f rebound, 7f settle, 6f still beat, then the same beat mirrored. The last keyframe is at f100, and with the 8f tail the loop is 108f = 1.8 s.
seamless: It returns exactly to rest with no symmetry needed. Both parts have p=[0,0] and r=0 at frames 0, 38, 50, 56, 88 and 100, and the engine holds rest through the 8-frame tail to op=108. Replaying it with the engine's own valueAt/bezier maths, frame 0 and frame 108 match for both parts. Both frames measure the seam gap at 3.807 to 3.820u across x=79 to 121, with a minimum part distance of 3.807u.

critic.distinct: Mostly distinct. A hinged wedge that switches sides reads differently from 001's clasp and from the current parallel tug. The risk is 004 (bracket jaws parting vertically): if the hinge end doesn't visibly hold still, both halves just tilt apart and it reads as jaws. As drafted the hinge end doesn't hold (see ROOTED), so right now it sits too close to 004.
critic.rooted: The fulcrum premise is wrong, and I checked it against the real path data. There are no 3.81u notches at the left and right mid-edges. The flat seam edges run only from x 79.48 to 120.52, where they meet the lobe arcs at a tangent. Out at (140,100) and (60,100) the lobes are fully round, so those points are empty space about 19u beyond the end of the seam. Sampling both paths about F=(140,100) at 2.73 deg, the seam at full open measures 5.66 / 7.62 / 9.57u at x=121 / 100 / 80, and the minimum part gap is 5.61u. The hinge end opens by half a module, so no point of the cut stays pinned. It reads as two halves tipping apart, not a clevis on its pin. Everything else is well rooted: the D2 mirrors, the module-sized amplitude and the no-overlap rule.
critic.craft: The timing structure is good: 18f open, a short hold, an accelerating 8f clap, then the mirrored beat, 1.8 s in all. The recoil interval (f38 to f43) starts with SOFT, which leaves at zero velocity. Right after an ease-in that arrives at about 4.5x speed, the clap looks like it sticks, pauses and then lifts again, rather than rebounding. The rebound should leave with velocity.

name: Corolla
story: All five petals slide outward at the same moment, each one along the straight slit it shares with its clockwise neighbour. The corolla opens like a camera aperture: the five channels widen and stay perfectly parallel, and the pentagonal eye grows and turns slightly. Then the blades snap shut, press a hair past rest and settle. It only works because this mark's gaps are straight, parallel 1.27u slits running almost through the centre, so each petal is a blade that can glide along its neighbour's edge. That shared edge is the "borrows its neighbor's edge" line from the blurb, put into motion.
character: Five hollow teardrop loops with their narrow ends aimed at an open pentagonal eye. It reads as a five-petal corolla (forget-me-not, plumeria) drawn in one pen weight. Each petal is a ribbon looped once, with both ends meeting at the tip, so the mark also suggests a rosette of five ribbon loops or a knot drawn by a draughtsman. Because the counter is a teardrop whose point touches the open centre, each petal also looks like a vessel or droplet with a mouth at the middle. It feels compass-made and patient: exact tangents, a 3:5 ring, and 1.27u channels held perfectly parallel. There is no real overlap anywhere. It is five separate bodies packed into five 72 deg wedges so tightly that they read as one flower.
symmetry: Dihedral D5. The true pivot is (100.25, 102.6), not (100,100). Rotating the point set 72/144/216/288 deg about (100.25,102.6) gives a mean nearest-point error of 0.065u (max 0.39, from sampling). Control angles (36, 60, 90, 120, 180 deg) give 2.2-2.9u. Rotating 72 deg about the nominal (100,100) gives 1.82u mean and 3.1u max, so a spin about the viewBox centre visibly wobbles. There are five mirror axes, each running through one petal's long axis (90, 18, -54, 126, 162 deg; error 0.066-0.086u). The between-petal axes (0 and 36 deg) fail at 2.9u. The vertical mirror sits at x = 100.28. The bbox is 59.03-141.58 x 60.00-140.06, so its centre (100.3, 100.03) is the point the construction used. A pentagon's bbox centre sits above its rotation centre, which accounts for the 2.6u offset. All five petals are congruent: area 460.3-461.7 each, radial extent r 11.54 to 42.6 from the true pivot.
construction: Each petal is one exact construction: two concentric circles, outer R 15.38 and counter R 9.22 (fit deviation under 0.015u). The ratio is 3:5, and the stroke is 6.16 = 2/5 R. Each circle gets a pair of tangent lines at +/-36 deg to the petal axis, so the legs meet at a 72 deg apex pointing at the pivot, which is exactly the 360/5 pitch. Measured tangency: the outer leg line is 15.36 from the ring centre and the inner leg line is 9.20. The legs are parallel strips of the same 6.16 width as the ring, so the whole petal reads as a single monoline loop. The counter's V apex is 9.22/sin36 = 15.69 below the ring centre, which puts it at r 11.53 from the pivot. The flat tip truncation is at r 11.55, so the counter's point lands exactly on the cut edge and the two legs touch there at one point (100.25, 91.05). Ring centres sit on an orbit of r 27.22 about (100.25,102.6), with adjacent ring centres 2 x 27.22 x sin36 = 32.0 apart. The rings are 30.76 across, which leaves a 1.24u kiss gap on the bisector at r 22.0. The outer legs of neighbouring petals are parallel lines 1.27u apart (measured 1.22-1.32), so every gap between petals is one straight radial slit of constant width, running from the pentagon corner at r 13.8 out to the ring kiss at r 22.0 before the arcs peel apart. Extended, the outer tangents pass about 0.63u from the pivot. The five flat tips (each 15.2 wide) bound a central pentagonal void with apothem 11.55, and the slits open its corners. Reconciling with the construction notes: spec R 15.4 matches (15.38) and pitch 72 deg matches. The con orbit circle (r 25.6, centre 100,100) and spec 'orbit R 26u' are drawn about the bbox centre. Measured from the true pivot the orbit is 27.22; measured from (100,100) the ring centres sit at 24.6 to 29.5. The con top-ring guide at (100.3,75.5) r 15.4 matches the measured (100.27,75.38) r 15.38. The blurb's 'each ring borrows its neighbor's edge' is the shared 1.27u radial slit: each petal's leg and its neighbour's leg are the same line doubled.
tensions: Most of the tension is in the five 1.27u radial slits. Each is about 8u long (r 13.8 to 22.0) and ends where the rings nearly kiss (1.24u), so the petals look pressed flank to flank, and any tangential move would collide at once. The second pinch point is each petal tip, where the two legs meet at a single point (0.02u) exactly on the pentagon cut. The loop is closed only at the tip, and the counter opens straight into the central void. The weight sits outboard: the rings (r 12 to 42.6) hold nearly all the ink and the centre is empty, so the mark is rim-heavy, like a wheel or a bloom with no core. The tangent legs make each petal a wedge pointing inward, so at rest the petals seem to be pulled toward the centre along their axes and held apart only by the slits. The 2.6u gap between the bbox centre and the true pivot is a hidden trap: any rotation or scale must use (100.25,102.6), or the flower will drift and the slits will visibly go unequal.
parts: petal loop, top (axis 270 deg / straight up)
ties: Which parts move: all five, together and unstaggered. The five petals are congruent (area 460.3-461.7) and placed with D5 symmetry, so the same slide on every petal keeps the 72 deg rotational symmetry exact. Numerically, C5 error at full open is 0.065u, the same as at rest. This also keeps it clear of 050's petal-by-petal bloom and 002's staggered ripple.

Direction: each petal translates along its petal axis +36 deg (screen-clockwise). The legs meet at a 72 deg apex, so each outer leg runs at +/-36 deg to the axis. That makes the clockwise leg parallel to the between-petal bisector: it is the radial slit, passing 0.63u from the pivot. The petal glides along its own leg line, so that side of the slit shears lengthwise instead of pulling apart.

Collision-free by construction: a move along the axis+36 direction pulls each petal away from its counter-clockwise neighbour's slit by sin72 = 0.951 per unit, and nothing moves toward anything. Every slit stays two parallel lines, with width 1.27 + 0.951*d. Measured minimum neighbour gaps at d = 3.2 are 4.29-4.38u (predicted 4.31), and the ring kiss gap never closes.

No rotation or scale, only translation. Pure translation keeps every leg line parallel to its old self, so all five channels stay constant-width strips the whole time, which is the mark's defining tension. It also keeps the move distinct from the current swirl-and-dip 'close' and from the spins owned by 038/086.

Axis snapping: the recipe rounds each part's bbox-centre bearing from the true pivot (100.25,102.6) to 270 + 72n. The bbox centre sits up to 0.67 deg off the true axis for rotated petals. The pentagon's bbox centre (100,100) is 2.6u off the rotation centre, so bearings are never taken from C. Verified axes: parts 0..4 = 270, 198, 342, 126, 54 deg.

Amplitude d = 3.08u = half the 6.16u monoline stroke, so each blade slides half its own pen width along its neighbour. That widens the slits from 1.27u to about 4.2u (roughly 3.3x, easy to read at thumbnail size). The radial component cos36*3.08 = 2.49u grows the central pentagon's apothem from 11.55 to about 14.0. The outer rim goes from r 42.6 to about 45.1, a restrained 6% swell.

Overshoot -0.3u along the same slit: on the close, the blades press 0.3u past rest, so the channels narrow to about 1.0u (measured 0.91-1.0 at -0.35, still clear) before settling. This is the 'seat' of iris blades closing, sized well under the 1.27u slit so nothing touches.

Chirality as the visible event: at full open the vertical mirror (x = 100.28) fails at 2.08u, so the five mirror axes switch off and the flower reads as a pinwheel. It returns to full D5 only at rest.

Easing and timing: GLIDE open over 32f (slow leave, soft arrival, like blades on a pin). HOLD 14f between identical values while the open eye reads. SNAP close over 22f (fast leave, firm catch) into the -0.3 seat. SOFT settle over 16f. There is one p track per part, and all parts share times and easings, so the engine runs native beziers.
seamless: It needs no symmetry argument. Every part's offset is exactly [0,0] at frame 0 (the track holds its first keyframe, [0,0] at f8) and exactly [0,0] at the last keyframe (f92), held through the 8-frame tail. There are no r or s tracks, so frames 0 and 100 are the identity transform and pixel-identical to rest. The in-between states keep exact C5 symmetry about (100.25,102.6), measured at 0.065u error, the same as the rest geometry.

critic.distinct: Distinct. All five petals move in unison with a chiral shear along the slit, so it is neither 050's petal-by-petal bloom nor 002's staggered radial push. Moving off the radial by 36 deg also keeps it from reading as the index's own Explode toggle. It replaces the current staggered swirl cleanly.
critic.rooted: Yes. The move direction comes from the 72 deg tangent apex: the clockwise leg line is the slit, and it passes 0.63u from the pivot. I verified the maths. Petal θ slides along its θ+36 leg line, so that slit wall stays collinear, while the neighbour's wall retreats at cos18 = 0.951 per unit. That gives the visible 'blade gliding on its neighbour's edge' detail, where one wall of each slit stays put. The axis snap from the true pivot (100.25,102.6) returns 270/198/342/126/54 for the analysis's part centres, which is correct. Amplitude = half the 6.16 stroke, and the overshoot is sized under the 1.27 slit (it narrows to about 0.98u, still clear).
critic.craft: Restrained and premium: GLIDE open over 32f, an eased HOLD read, a SNAP close into a -0.3u seat (10% of amplitude), then a SOFT settle. 1.67 s, a single p track, native beziers. Nothing bouncy. The only watch-item is that the chirality comes from a 1.81u tangential component, so it will read as the slits opening and the eye widening more than as a pinwheel. That's acceptable, and arguably the right restraint.

name: Latitude
story: The whole disc turns over once like a coin, on the axle the drawing already has: the horizontal line through the two points where the equator touches the rim, at 9 and 3 o'clock. Rim and rings foreshorten together. The mark spools up slowly, snaps through edge-on, where it vanishes for about a frame, then opens out mirrored and coasts to a stop with no overshoot. Only this mark can land upside down and look unchanged, because it is symmetric about its own equator.
character: A small globe seen slightly from above, with three identical rings. They could be latitudes, but the equal heights and even pitch also make it read like a coiled spring or a slinky held sideways inside a porthole. It is calm and horizontal: every internal line runs east-west, and the only vertical reading comes from the stacking. Because the equator ring is inscribed tangent to the rim at 9 and 3 o'clock, the whole globe seems pinned on an invisible horizontal axle through (54,100) and (146,100), like a gimballed instrument, an armillary or a gyro in its cage. The fused top and bottom latitudes make the poles feel like solid caps, while the middle is open and airy. It is Meridian's level-headed sibling. Where Meridian's lines would divide the globe, these lines layer it.
symmetry: Dihedral D2. I rotated and mirrored the sampled outline point set and measured the worst-case nearest-point error. Vertical mirror at x=100: max 0.11u (mean 0.003). Horizontal mirror at y=100: max 0.12u (mean 0.03). 180 degree rotation: max 0.12u. Any other order fails: 90 degrees gives 7.1u max error, 60 degrees 7.1u, 45 degrees 6.9u. So the rotational order is exactly 2. The mark returns to itself after a half turn in the plane and also after a flip about the horizontal equator axis. The flip is the less obvious symmetry, and the motion ideas depend on it.
construction:
The wrapper is translate(54,54) scale(1.3143). The local 70-unit box maps to mark 54..146, the local centre (35,35) maps to (100,100), and the outer radius is 46u, matching con. Every stroke is the same weight: 2.258 local, which is 2.97u.

The mark has four rings: the rim plus three horizontal ellipse outlines. The spec's "4 latitudes" is really the rim plus three latitudes.
(a) Equator ellipse, centred at (100,100). Outer semi-axes 46 x 16.33, inner 43.03 x 13.36, aspect about 2.82:1. Its horizontal extremes coincide with the rim at (54,100) and (146,100), so it is inscribed and tangent there, fused into the rim.
(b) Top latitude, centred at (100,82.55). Inner semi-axes 38.9 x 13.36, outer half-height 16.33, the same height as the equator. Its sides are buried in the rim stroke: the inner edge comes within 0.45u of the rim's inner edge at y 82.55.
(c) Bottom latitude, the mirror image, centred at (100,117.45).

The centre pitch is uniform at 17.45u. That is less than the ellipse outer height of 32.66u, so neighbours overlap by about 15.2u. Each overlap makes an X crossing on the flanks at about (100 +/- 34, 100 +/- 9.6), roughly 12u in from the rim, with small curved-triangle holes wedged between each crossing and the rim. The top and bottom latitudes never cross. Their facing arcs nearly kiss at dead centre: 98.86 vs 101.14, a 2.29u gap sitting on (100,100). Above the top latitude, the top ellipse's upper arc and the rim close off a polar lens hole, 65.9 wide and 9.26 tall at the centre line; the bottom lens mirrors it.

Reconciling with the notes:
- Con's R 46u is exact.
- Con's "LAT +/-5.3U +/-12.7U" guides are not the ellipse centres. They match the bbox centroids of the visible arc fragments: +/-5.22 for the inner kissing arcs (paths 3 and 4) and +/-12.81 for the equator arcs (paths 1 and 2). The true ellipse centres are 0 and +/-17.45.
- The blurb's claim that the rings "compress toward the poles at true projection" is not supported. All three ellipses have identical half-heights (13.36 inner), and the spacing is even. Only the width shrinks, 43.03 to 38.9 (0.904x). A true orthographic globe would shrink both axes and bunch the spacing toward the poles.
- This is an idealised, evenly pitched stack. It reads as latitudes on a globe tilted about 20.8 degrees toward the viewer: asin(16.33/46) = 0.355 rad, about 20.8 degrees.
tensions:
1) The waist kiss. The top and bottom latitudes' facing arcs almost meet across a 2.29u gap exactly on the mark centre. This is the loudest near-touch in the mark: the centre reads as a pinched hourglass lying on its side, a place that wants to seal.
2) Flank crossings. The four X-crossings at (100 +/- 34, 100 +/- 9.6) are where line density peaks, so the visual weight sits on the left and right shoulders, not the centre.
3) Pole weight. The latitudes' outer arcs merge into the rim and leave only thin lens holes (9.26u tall), so the top and bottom read heavier and more closed than the open equatorial window.
4) Hinge points. The equator is tangent to the rim at (54,100) and (146,100). These two points are the only places where an interior ring and the rim share a boundary cleanly, and they imply an axle.
5) The flatness itself. The 2.82:1 aspect encodes a tilt of about 20.8 degrees. At rest the mark already implies it is part-way through a nod, neither edge-on nor face-on.
6) Uniform stroke (2.97u everywhere) plus even pitch give no single dominant ring. The energy comes from overlap, not hierarchy.
parts: Frame: the R46 rim fused with the outer arcs of the top and bottom latitude ellipses. It has three counter-wound holes: a top polar lens, a bottom polar lens and the large central window
Top latitude ellipse, lower arc (the arc that dips toward the centre)
Bottom latitude ellipse, upper arc (the arc that rises toward the centre)
ties: Which parts move: all five, as one rigid body with identical tracks. Part 0 fuses the rim with the latitudes' outer arcs and flank pieces. Parts 1-4 meet it and each other at the flank crossings (100 +/- 34, 100 +/- 9.6), so moving any arc on its own opens a seam there. The only clean motion is the whole mark, which is also Jean's stated preference.

Axis: horizontal, through y = 100. The equator ellipse is inscribed tangent to the rim at (54,100) and (146,100), which is the only clean shared boundary between an interior ring and the rim. Those two points define the axle.

Pivot: C = (100,100). This is the midpoint of the two tangent points and lies exactly on the flip axis, so nothing translates. The waist kiss (the 2.29u gap between parts 3 and 4) also sits on this point, so the mark folds flat through its own tightest spot.

Amplitude: exactly 180 degrees and no more. The rotational order is exactly 2 and the horizontal mirror holds (0.12u max by the analysis, 0.087u max and 0.026 mean on a 5158-point resample), so a half flip lands on a pose that matches the rest pose. The overrun is gone: orthographic foreshortening is even about 180, so any angle past it shortens the height again and reads as a vertical squash, not a lean.

The event is the cos snap through zero. Half-height is 46*|cos(x)|: 39.1u at f28, 24.9u at f32, 12.3u at f34, 5.0u at f35, 2.3u at f36 (mirrored), 9.2u at f37, 25.4u at f40. The zero crossing falls at f35.7. There the y-scale is zero, every fill collapses to zero area and the mark vanishes for about one frame. It is not a hairline. That snap is what makes it read as a rotation rather than a scaleY squash or a blink.
Direction: the sign doesn't matter visually, because +x and -x foreshorten identically. There is no wind-back, since an anticipation dip would read as a height stutter before the flip.

Easing: one interval, INERTIA from f8 to f72. It gives a heavy spool-up (only 16.9 degrees by f24), a fast middle (f28 to f44 covers 31.9 to 143.5 degrees) and a long soft arrival (179.59 degrees at f68, per-frame deltas 0.30 -> 0.18 -> 0.08 -> 0.02). INERTIA already lands softly, so no SOFT settle segment is needed.
Length: last keyframe f72, plus the engine's 8 hold frames, gives op = 80 = 1.33 s. This is inside the 1.2-2.2 s window and shorter than the current 98-frame spin.
seamless: Frame 0 is the identity. From f72 through op f80 the pose is pitch 180 about y = 100, i.e. scale(1,-1) about C, which is the mirror (x, y) -> (x, 200 - y). The mark is D2 symmetric and its horizontal mirror maps the union onto itself: part 0 maps to itself, 1 swaps with 2 (mean y 112.15 <-> 87.86) and 3 swaps with 4 (93.11 <-> 106.71). The worst-case error is 0.087u on the resample (0.12u by the analysis), under 3% of the 2.97u stroke, so it is invisible when the engine drops the transform at the end (fill: none). Mirroring every subpath reverses its winding uniformly, so the nonzero fill is unchanged. Arrival velocity is effectively zero: 179.59 degrees at f68, 180.0 at f72, and cos 179.59 = -0.99997 is a 0.001u height difference.

critic.distinct: The verb (pitch about the equator axle) isn't on the owned list and differs from 038's in-plane spin and from 089 and 095, so it is distinct in principle.
critic.rooted: The flip itself is rooted in the horizontal mirror (0.087u), and the axle through the tangent points at (54,100) and (146,100) is real. But the story contradicts what the transform does. scale(s, s*cos x) foreshortens part 0, the rim, as well. A globe's silhouette never flattens, and a gimbal's cage doesn't turn with the ring, so what plays is a flat coin flip, not a globe in its cage. The motion idea in its own analysis says the rim should stay still. At the edge-on frame the mark doesn't become 'a single hairline': zero y-scale collapses every fill to zero area, so the mark vanishes for about 1-2 frames.
critic.craft: The 200.8 deg overrun is a squash bounce, not a lean. Orthographic foreshortening is even about 180 (the draft concedes the sign doesn't matter), so the height runs 1 → 0 → 1 → 0.935 → 1. The mark lands at full height, drops 3u, then stretches back. That is exactly the squash-and-stretch this catalogue avoids. The INERTIA spool into the flip is good.
